questions.question:
Consider the statement
"Not all that glitters is gold"
Predicate glitters(x) is true if x glitters and predicate gold(x) is true if x is gold. Which one of the following logical formulae represents the above statement?
questions.explanation:
"Not all that glitters is gold" means: there is something that glitters but is not gold.

[latex] eg orall x\,(glitters(x)\Rightarrow gold(x))\equiv\exists x\,(glitters(x)\wedge eg gold(x))[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\exists x: glitters(x)\wedge eg gold(x)[/latex]

questions.question: Let G=(V,E) be a directed graph where V is the set of vertices and E the set of edges. Then which one of the following graphs has the same strongly connected components as G ?

options.C: [latex]G_{3}=(V,E_{3})[/latex] where [latex]E_{3}\equiv \{(u,v)|[/latex] there is a path of lenth [latex]\leq[/latex] 2 from u to v in E}
options.D: [latex]G_{4}=(V_{4},E)[/latex] where [latex]V_{4}[/latex]  is the set of vertices in G which are not isolated

questions.explanation:
Reversing every edge keeps every cycle (just traversed backwards). If u and v can reach each other in G, they still can in the reversed graph, so the strongly connected components are the same.

The complement graph, the "paths of length [latex]\le[/latex] 2" graph and removing isolated vertices can all change the SCCs.

Answer: [latex]G_2[/latex] with all edges reversed

Check the 4th equation: [latex]-[/latex]2.2 [latex]-[/latex] 7.6 + 9.8 = 0 True. So the system is consistent with exactly one solution.

questions.question:
Let the function
[latex]f(\theta)=\begin{vmatrix} sin\theta & cos\theta & tan\theta \\ sin(\frac{\pi}{6}) & cos(\frac{\pi}{6}) & tan(\frac{\pi}{6})\\ sin(\frac{\pi}{3})& cos(\frac{\pi}{3}) & tan(\frac{\pi}{3}) \end{vmatrix}[/latex]
where [latex]\theta \in [\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{3}][/latex] and [latex]f'(\theta )[/latex] denote the derivative of f with respect to [latex]\theta[/latex] . Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
(I) There existrs [latex]\theta \in (\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{3})[/latex] such that [latex]f'(\theta )=0[/latex]
(I) There existrs [latex]\theta \in (\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{3})[/latex] such that [latex]f'(\theta )\neq 0[/latex]
questions.explanation:
At [latex]\theta=\pi/6[/latex] the first row equals the second, and at [latex]\theta=\pi/3[/latex] it equals the third, so [latex]f(\pi/6)=f(\pi/3)=0[/latex].

- By Rolle's theorem, [latex]f'(\theta)=0[/latex] somewhere in between [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] I true.
- f is not constant, so [latex]f'(\theta)\ne0[/latex] somewhere [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] II true.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.question:
The base (or radix) of the number system such that the following equation holds is_______.
[latex]\frac{312}{20}=13.1[/latex]

In base b: [latex]312=3b^2+b+2[/latex], [latex]20=2b[/latex], [latex]13.1=b+3+\frac1b[/latex].
[latex]3b^2+b+2=2b\left(b+3+\frac1b\right)=2b^2+6b+2\Rightarrow b^2=5b\Rightarrow b=5[/latex]

questions.question:
Let G be a graph with n vertices and m edges. What is the tightest upper bound on the
running time of Depth First Search on G, when G is represented as an adjacency matrix?
questions.explanation:
With an adjacency matrix, finding the neighbours of a vertex means scanning its whole row of n entries. DFS does this for every vertex: [latex]n\times n=\Theta(n^2)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n^2)[/latex]

questions.question:
Consider rooted n node binary tree represented using pointers. The best upper bound on the
time required to determine the number of sub trees having exactly 4 nodes is [latex]O(n^{a}lob^{b}n)[/latex] .
Then the value of a+10b is_______
questions.explanation:
A post-order traversal computes the size of every subtree (1 + left size + right size) in [latex]O(n)[/latex] total, and counts subtrees of size 4 along the way.

[latex]O(n)=O(n^1\log^0 n)[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a = 1, b = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a + 10b = 1

Answer: 1

options.D: The language L = { ww| w[latex]\in \Sigma^{*}[/latex] with [latex]\Sigma[/latex]={0,1}} is regular.

Answer: The language with 3k+1 b's is regular

questions.question:
Suppose a disk has 201 cylinders, numbered from 0 to 200. At some time the disk arm is at
cylinder 100, and there is a queue of disk access requests for cylinders 30, 85, 90, 100, 105,
110, 135 and 145. If Shortest-Seek Time First (SSTF) is being used for scheduling the disk
access, the request for cylinder 90 is serviced after servicing ____________ number of
requests.
questions.explanation:
SSTF from 100: 100 (distance 0), then 105 (5), then 110 (5), then 90 (20, closer than 135 at 25).

So 90 is served after 3 requests.

Answer: 3

questions.question: Which one of the following is FALSE?

options.A: User level threads are not scheduled by the kernel
options.B: When a user level thread is blocked, all other threads of its process are blocked.
options.C:
Context switching between user level threads is faster than context switching between
kernel level threads.
options.D: Kernel level threads cannot share the code segment

questions.explanation:
Kernel threads of the same process share the code segment (and data, files); only their stacks and registers are separate. So "kernel level threads cannot share the code segment" is false.

Answer: Kernel level threads cannot share the code segment

questions.question:
Given the following statements:
S1: A foreign key declaration can always be replaced by an equivalent check assertion in SQL
S2: Given the table R(a,b,c) where a and b together form the primary key, the following is a valid table definition.
CREATE TABLE S (
a INTEGER,
d INTEGER,
e INTEGER,
PRIMARY KEY (d),
FOREIGN KEY (a) references R)
Which one of the following statements is CORRECT?

options.A: S1 is TRUE and S2 is a FALSE
options.B: Both S1 and S2 are TRUE
options.C: S1 is FALSE and S2 is a TRUE
options.D: Both S1 and S2 are FALSE

questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- S1: a CHECK constraint cannot always replace a foreign key (it cannot easily refer to another table and handle updates/deletes) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] FALSE.
- S2: R's primary key is (a, b), so a foreign key must reference both columns; FOREIGN KEY (a) references R is invalid [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: Both S1 and S2 are FALSE

questions.question:
Consider the following three statements about link state and distance vector routing protocols, for a large network with 500 network nodes and 4000 links
[S1] The computational overhead in link state protocols is higher than in distance vector protocols.
[S2] A distance vector protocol (with split horizon) avoids persistent routing loops, but not a link state protocol.
[S3] After a topology change, a link state protocol will converge faster than a distance vector protocol.
Which one of the following is correct about S1, S2, and S3?

options.A: S1, S2, and S3 are all true
options.B: S1, S2, and S3 are all false.
options.C: S1 and S2 are true, but S3 is false
options.D: S1 and S3 are true, but S2 is false.

questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- S1: each link-state router runs Dijkstra on the whole topology [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] more computation True
- S2: split horizon does not prevent all loops (count-to-infinity can still happen), while link-state avoids persistent loops False
- S3: link-state floods updates and recomputes at once [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] faster convergence True

Answer: S1 and S3 are true, but S2 is false

questions.question: Consider a token ring network with a length of 2km having 10 stations including a monitoring station. The propagation speed of the signal is 2x[latex]10^{8}[/latex] m/s and the token transmission time is ignored. If each station is allowed to hold the token for 2 [latex]\mu[/latex]sec, the minimum time for which the monitoring station should wait (in [latex]\mu[/latex]sec) before assuming that the token is lost is _______.
questions.explanation:
Propagation around the ring = 2000 / ([latex]2\times10^8[/latex]) = 10 [latex]\mu[/latex]s. In the worst case each of the other 9 stations holds the token for 2 [latex]\mu[/latex]s = 18 [latex]\mu[/latex]s.

Wait at least 10 + 18 = 28 [latex]\mu[/latex]s (30 [latex]\mu[/latex]s if the monitor's own holding time is counted; both are accepted).

Answer: 28

questions.question: Let the size of congestion window of a TCP connection be 32 KB when a timeout occurs. The round trip time of the connection is 100 msec and the maximum segment size used is 2kB. The time taken (in msec) by the TCP connection to get back to 32KB congestion window is ______

After the timeout: ssthresh = 16 KB, cwnd = 2 KB (1 MSS).
- Slow start: 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 16 KB (3 RTTs)
- Congestion avoidance, +2 KB per RTT: 18, 20, [latex]\ldots[/latex], 32 KB (8 RTTs)

Total 11 RTTs [latex]\times[/latex] 100 ms = 1100 ms

Answer: 1100

questions.question:
Consider a selective repeat sliding window protocol that uses a frame size of 1 KB to send
data on a 1.5 Mbps link with a one-way latency of 50 msec. To achieve a link utilization of
60%, the minimum number of bits required to represent the sequence number field is ________.
questions.explanation:
Frame time = 8192 / 1.5 Mbps [latex]\approx[/latex] 5.46 ms; one cycle = 5.46 + 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 50 = 105.46 ms.
For 60% utilization: [latex]W\times5.46=0.6\times105.46\Rightarrow W\approx11.6[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 12 frames.

Selective repeat needs [latex]2^{k-1}\ge12\Rightarrow k=5[/latex] bits.

Answer: 5

There are 3 units of type X, 2 units of type Y and 2 units of type Z still available. The system is currently in a safe state. Consider the following independent requests for additional resources in the current state:
REQ1: P0 requests 0 units of X, 0 units of Y and 2 units of Z
REQ2: P1 requests 2 units of x, 0 units of Y and 0 units of Z
Which one of the following is TRUE?

options.C: Both REQ1 and REQ2 can be permitted
options.D: Neither REQ1 nor REQ2 can be permitted

questions.question: Let L be a language and [latex]\bar{L}[/latex] be its complement. Which of the following is NOT a viable possibility?

If both L and [latex]\bar L[/latex] are r.e., running their recognizers in parallel decides L, so L is recursive. "Both r.e. but not recursive" is therefore impossible; the other three cases do occur.

questions.question: Suppose a polynomial time algorithm is discovered that correctly computes the largest clique in a given graph. In this scenario, which one of the following represents the correct Venn diagram of the complexity classes P, NP and NP Complete (NPC)?
questions.explanation:
Max-clique is NP-hard, so a polynomial algorithm for it would give P = NP. Then every non-trivial problem in NP is NP-complete, so the classes coincide: P = NP = NPC.

Answer: D

questions.question:
Consider the following pseudo code. What is the total number of multiplications to be performed? 
 D= 2
for i = 1 to n do
   for j = i to n do
      for k = j + 1 to n do
           D = D * 3

options.A: Half of the product of the 3 consecutive integers
options.B: One-third of the product of the 3 consecutive integers.
options.C: One-sixth of the product of the 3 consecutive integers

questions.explanation:
For fixed i and j the innermost loop runs n [latex]-[/latex] j times. Summing over [latex]1\le i\le j\le n[/latex] gives [latex]\binom{n+1}{3}=\frac{(n-1)n(n+1)}{6}[/latex].

That is one-sixth of the product of 3 consecutive integers.

Answer: One-sixth of the product of the 3 consecutive integers

questions.question:
Consider a 6-stage instruction pipeline, where all stages are perfectly balanced. Assume that
there is no cycle-time overhead of pipelining. When an application is executing on this 6-stage pipeline, the speedup achieved with respect to non-pipelined execution if 25% of the instructions incur 2 pipeline stall cycles is _________.
questions.explanation:
Pipelined CPI = 1 + 0.25 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 = 1.5. A balanced 6-stage pipeline ideally gives speedup 6.

Speedup = 6 / 1.5 = 4

Answer: 4

questions.question:
An access sequence of cache block addresses is of length N and contains n unique block
addresses. The number of unique block addresses between two consecutive accesses to the
same block address is bounded above K. What is the miss ratio if the access sequence is
passed through a cache of associativity A[latex]\geq[/latex]k exercising least-recently-used replacement policy?
questions.explanation:
Between two uses of the same block, at most k other blocks are used, and the cache holds A [latex]\ge[/latex] k blocks per set with LRU. So a block is never evicted before it is used again: only the first access to each of the n distinct blocks misses.

Miss ratio = n / N

Answer: n/N

questions.question:
A function f(x) is continuous in the interval [0,2]. It is known that f(0)=f(2)=-1 and f(1)=1.
Which one of the following statements must be true?

options.A: There exists a y in the interval (0,1) such that f(y)=f(y+1)
options.B: For every y in the interval (0,1), f(y)=f(2-y)
options.C: The maximum value of the function in the interval (0.2) is 1
options.D: There exists a y in the interval (0,1) such that f(y)=-f(2-y)

questions.explanation:
Let g(y) = f(y) [latex]-[/latex] f(y + 1) on [0, 1]. g(0) = f(0) [latex]-[/latex] f(1) = [latex]-[/latex]2 and g(1) = f(1) [latex]-[/latex] f(2) = 2. g is continuous and changes sign, so g(y) = 0 for some y in (0, 1), i.e. f(y) = f(y + 1).

Answer: There exists a y in (0,1) such that f(y)=f(y+1)

questions.question: An ordered n-tuple ([latex]d_{1}, d_{2} ,... , d_{n}[/latex]) with [latex]d_{1}\geq d_{2} \geq ... \geq d_{n}[/latex] is called graphic if there exists a simple undirected graph with n vertices having degrees [latex]d_{1}, d_{2} ,... , d_{n}[/latex] respectively. questions.explanation:
(3, 3, 3, 1, 0, 0): ignore the two isolated vertices, leaving 4 vertices with degrees 3, 3, 3, 1. Each degree-3 vertex must connect to all three others, so the fourth vertex would have degree 3, not 1. Not graphic.

Answer: (3, 3, 3, 1, 0, 0)

Which one of the following propositional logic formulas is TRUE when exactly two of p, q,
and r are TRUE?
questions.explanation:
Exactly two true means either r is true with exactly one of p, q (that is [latex]\neg(p\leftrightarrow q)\wedge r[/latex]), or p and q true with r false ([latex]p\wedge q\wedge\sim r[/latex]). Option 2 is exactly the OR of these two cases.

questions.explanation:
